QF.id: III-C Prevention of Money Laundering Act_34

question.text: In the FIU Delhi vs PayPal case, the total fine imposed on PayPal was Rs. 96 lakh. If this was imposed at the maximum per-failure penalty of Rs. 1 lakh under Section 13(2)(d) of PMLA, this represents a minimum of how many individual failures?

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 13(2)(d) of PMLA allows a monetary penalty that may extend to Rs. 1 lakh for each failure (NISM-Series-III-C workbook, p.163). Page 179 records that the FIU imposed a total fine of Rs. 96 lakh on PayPal under Section 13(2)(d). Treating the entire fine as imposed at the maximum Rs. 1 lakh per failure gives a hypothetical minimum of 96 failures (96,00,000 / 1,00,000 = 96). The Trap: 48 and 10 fail the arithmetic; "Cannot be determined" overlooks the calculation explicitly assumed by the stem. Note: The 96 figure here is a hypothetical minimum from the per-failure cap on p.163, not a count of individual failures stated in the source — p.179 frames the violations as three broad counts described as deliberate and wilful contraventions.
